## Task T06 (narrative: work/T06/report.md)

### Arguments (3)

#### A-T06-001 — Alexander’s brain-independence argument (position: Strongest conditional reconstruction, not endorsed conclusion)

- Premises: Elaborate experience was remembered., If relevant brain processes were excluded during that experience, a specified ordinary production account would fail., Claimed external details and prior description might strengthen accuracy if independently verified.
- Bridge principles: Retrospective memory accurately dates its content to the excluded interval., Clinical evidence rules out all processes required by the targeted model., Alternate ordinary information routes do not explain verified details.
- Conclusion: Conditional support for H-B; no automatic H-S/H-T or deity inference
- Claims: CL-T06-002, CL-T06-005, CL-T06-007, CL-T06-008, CL-T06-013, CL-T06-016, CL-T06-018; sources: S-T06-001, S-T06-005, S-T06-006
- Strongest objection: A-T06-002: neither temporal alignment nor exclusion of all relevant processing is established.; strongest reply: Defender appeals to profound impairment, different recovery phenomenology and corroborative detail rather than credentials alone.
- Unresolved issues: Recoverable brain illness is not irreversible death. Even H-B needs a substrate definition; other physical realization is logically possible.
- Review: R06 (accept)

#### A-T06-002 — Underdetermination and ordinary alternatives (position: Audit reconstruction with Shermer’s original challenge)

- Premises: Reports and clinical severity do not directly identify the moment each memory formed., A feeling of reality alone cannot validate external objects., Ordinary mechanisms may remain possible without any one being demonstrated.
- Bridge principles: A claim that excludes a mechanism must establish the relevant exclusion, not rely solely on explanatory incompleteness.
- Conclusion: This packet does not identify a unique neural or non-neural cause
- Claims: CL-T06-006, CL-T06-009, CL-T06-012, CL-T06-013, CL-T06-019; sources: S-T06-001, S-T06-002, S-T06-008
- Strongest objection: A-T06-001: severe impairment and corroborated details could challenge a precisely specified brain-dependent account.; strongest reply: Preserve corroborative reports and propose independently dated/timed tests; do not declare hallucination merely because it is possible.
- Unresolved issues: Raw records and prospective synchronization absent. Comparator studies and direct Sacks source not inspected.
- Review: R06 (accept)

#### A-T06-003 — Severe illness versus solely pharmacological coma (position: Narrow dispute audit)

- Premises: Dittrich publishes Potter’s sedation/responsiveness account., Mays disputes its context., Clinical review attributes pre-sedation deterioration to illness while acknowledging mixed later contributions.
- Bridge principles: Different descriptions can concern different stages and mechanisms; quotations alone do not settle physiology.
- Conclusion: Avoid both drug-only dismissal and inference from serious illness to complete brain inactivity
- Claims: CL-T06-012, CL-T06-014, CL-T06-015; sources: S-T06-002, S-T06-003, S-T06-004
- Strongest objection: Witness accounts are retrospective and contested.; strongest reply: Published chart review strengthens severe-illness documentation but is not a continuous functional recording.
- Unresolved issues: Original interview and clinical chronology needed to settle remaining particulars.
- Review: R06 (accept)

## Task T19 (narrative: work/T19/report.md)

### Arguments (3)

#### A-T19-001 — Dentures conditional anomalous-perception argument (position: project-authored conditional inference map)

- Premises: In Smit’s translated nurse account, the patient later identifies TG and a distinctive cart/shelf associated with the dentures; investigators did not obtain a direct patient interview., Smit and Rivas acknowledge dependence on one principal witness and state that official medical records had been destroyed; the present audit has no measured EEG interval for the dentures perception., Smit and Rivas reply that TG placed dentures removal before restarting the Thumper, and that a pre-opened wooden shelf undermines an explanation relying on hearing a metal drawer.
- Bridge principles: A verified acquisition episode incompatible with a specified dependence model challenges that model only when timing, identity and information-access premises hold.
- Conclusion: If the report and exclusion/timing premises hold, the specific neural-dependence model would be challenged.
- Claims: CL-T19-004, CL-T19-005, CL-T19-006, CL-T19-007, CL-T19-008, CL-T19-009, CL-T19-010, CL-T19-011, CL-T19-012; sources: S-T19-002, S-T19-003, S-T19-004
- Strongest objection: Single-witness retrospective timing and information control are insufficient to establish those premises.; strongest reply: Unusual shelf details and pre-Thumper removal deserve testing; a generic ordinary possibility does not erase the report.
- Unresolved issues: No defensible numerical likelihood ratio or posterior; dependence on shared case narratives retained.
- Review: R19 (accept)

#### A-T19-002 — Reynolds conditional anomalous-perception argument (position: project-authored conditional inference map)

- Premises: Carter reproduces Reynolds’s descriptions of a toothbrush-like surgical tool, its case, a vessel-size exchange and an apparent encounter with relatives; the narrative and subsequent matching depend substantially on Sabom’s account., Carter explicitly places the externally checkable early perceptions before absent brainstem response; Hameroff conditionally agrees the four auditory examples occurred under anesthesia rather than hypothermic circulatory arrest., Carter argues that vivid visual details, the missing reported clicks, sealing/masking and brainstem-versus-conscious perception distinctions challenge Woerlee’s account, and proposes a calibrated reconstruction., Carter quotes Cordova on technical parameters and explicitly locates Cordova in the adjacent operating room; Cordova’s quoted statement calls for an experiment and does not itself establish whether Reynolds heard.
- Bridge principles: A verified acquisition episode incompatible with a specified dependence model challenges that model only when timing, identity and information-access premises hold.
- Conclusion: If precise perception and independently established exclusion conditions coincide, the case favors acquisition beyond the specified normal channels.
- Claims: CL-T19-013, CL-T19-014, CL-T19-015, CL-T19-016, CL-T19-017, CL-T19-018, CL-T19-019, CL-T19-020; sources: S-T19-005, S-T19-006, S-T19-007
- Strongest objection: Checkable claims occur outside the alleged standstill interval, and drug/monitoring/access conditions are incompletely inspected.; strongest reply: Carter’s technical details and visual specificity challenge simplistic hearing reconstructions; neither party has supplied the decisive controlled comparison here.
- Unresolved issues: No defensible numerical likelihood ratio or posterior; dependence on shared case narratives retained.
- Review: R19 (accept)

#### A-T19-003 — Limit of survival and cosmic extrapolation (position: project-authored conditional inference map)

- Premises: The two dossiers support specific, traceable perception claims and substantive disputes, but lack independently fixed perception timing plus complete information-access controls needed to identify extracerebral acquisition., Resuscitation reports do not by themselves establish the same person’s subjectivity beyond irreversible death, fundamental mind, universal subjecthood or timelessness.
- Bridge principles: Temporary independence does not automatically establish irreversible-death survival or cosmic/normative attributes.
- Conclusion: Neither dossier establishes the full enduring/timeless conscious-foundation package.
- Claims: CL-T19-021, CL-T19-022, CL-T19-023; sources: S-T19-001, S-T19-002, S-T19-003, S-T19-004, S-T19-005, S-T19-006, S-T19-007
- Strongest objection: A verified brain-independent episode could nevertheless be relevant to models permitting personal survival.; strongest reply: Relevance is retained conditionally; irreversible death, numerical identity, universal subjecthood, purpose and normative relations require additional premises.
- Unresolved issues: No defensible numerical likelihood ratio or posterior; dependence on shared case narratives retained.
- Review: R19 (accept)

#### A-P2T09-001 — EEG–recollection intersection challenge and direct reply (position: Critic and author exchange, with symmetric inference limits)

- Premises: CL-P2T09-002, CL-P2T09-003, CL-P2T09-004, CL-P2T09-014
- Bridge principles: Positive EEG–experience association requires an appropriate participant/time intersection., Absence of explicit memory is not equivalent to absence of consciousness.
- Conclusion: The main study does not establish the positive association, and the missing association does not establish that the EEG patterns cannot be consciousness markers.
- Claims: CL-P2T09-001, CL-P2T09-002, CL-P2T09-003, CL-P2T09-004, CL-P2T09-014, CL-P2T09-015, CL-P2T09-016; sources: S-P2T09-001, S-P2T09-002, S-T07-007
- Strongest objection: A plausible clinical EEG interpretation and implicit-memory analogy might support consciousness despite absent recall.; strongest reply: These possibilities rebut a negative inference but do not identify the content or timing of an experience in the monitored participants.
- Unresolved issues: Missing participant/time intersection Raw data and independent artifact classification Clinical marker validation in this protocol
- Review: R-P2R09 (accept)

#### A-P2T09-002 — From unusual recollection to extracerebral acquisition (position: Conditional favorable case and strongest methodological countercase)

- Premises: CL-P2T09-009, CL-P2T09-010, CL-P2T09-012, CL-P2T09-013, CL-P2T09-016, CL-P2T09-020
- Bridge principles: Externally accurate details would discriminate models only if timing and ordinary access were sufficiently constrained., Descriptive similarity or vividness does not establish external accuracy or the source of information.
- Conclusion: Investigative interest remains warranted, but the inspected versions and correspondence do not establish excluded-process perception or brain independence.
- Claims: CL-P2T09-005, CL-P2T09-009, CL-P2T09-010, CL-P2T09-012, CL-P2T09-013, CL-P2T09-016, CL-P2T09-020; sources: S-T07-001, S-T07-007, S-T07-004, S-P2T09-001, S-P2T09-002
- Strongest objection: Author-checked resuscitation details and preserved cognition despite severe physiological compromise are difficult for simple absence-of-consciousness assumptions.; strongest reply: Challenge to that simple assumption is not an exclusion of every brain-dependent account; subject-specific neural state, memory timing and ordinary information access remain unmeasured or unresolved.
- Depends on arguments: A-P2T09-001
- Unresolved issues: Participant-linked physiology and timing Independent contemporaneous record access Target opportunities and chance model No observation beyond irreversible death
- Review: R-P2R09 (accept)

#### A-P2T09-003 — Martial direct reply: explanatory limits and the fruit reference class (position: Strongest inspected110205defense with protocol comparison)

- Premises: CL-P2T09-006, CL-P2T09-022, CL-P2T09-023, CL-P2T09-024, CL-P2T09-025
- Bridge principles: Methodological constraints explain missing analysis but do not supply its result., A chance model must match the actual cue, response space, scoring and sampling dependence., Physiological change and subjective descriptions do not independently establish a proposed mechanism.
- Conclusion: The direct reply repairs debate coverage and offers a positive account; it does not close opportunity, timing, classification or guessing-model gaps.
- Claims: CL-P2T09-006, CL-P2T09-012, CL-P2T09-013, CL-P2T09-022, CL-P2T09-023, CL-P2T09-024, CL-P2T09-025; sources: S-T07-003, S-P2T09-005, S-T07-007
- Strongest objection: Clinical constraints and the rapidly changing state may make a stable-state critique inappropriate; standardized patterns and unusual responses may remain informative.; strongest reply: Their information value must be assessed within the available measurements and protocol; neither lack of detailed analysis nor a noun-count denominator establishes the needed inference.
- Depends on arguments: A-P2T09-001, A-P2T09-002
- Unresolved issues: Fruit-choice distribution and scoring Participant/time linkage Independent standards/classification validation 2022original critic and broader2025/2026chain remain uninspected
- Review: R-P2R09 (accept)

## Task P2T14 (narrative: work/P2T14/report.md)

### Arguments (3)

#### A-P2T14-001 — Vivid continuity and the reported Nelson–Barker exchange (position: Strongest conditional positive case with directly case-linked criticism and actual third-party reply)

- Premises: Neal’s testimony describes continuous, vivid awareness and apparent rescue perception; the experiential attribution is supported, its external accuracy is not thereby established., If independently fixed perceptions occurred without ordinary information access during measured absence of relevant brain function, this would challenge a strict dependence account., The memoir’s named rescuers and individually conducted retrospective interviews are a stronger positive lead than unnamed retelling, but they remain narrated method and testimony.
- Bridge principles: Move from seeming to external perception only with independent event/information controls., Move from elapsed rescue time to neural incapacity only with relevant physiological evidence.
- Conclusion: The positive case is worth exact documentation; the present packet supports attributed experience and a conditional argument, not survival.
- Claims: CL-P2T14-011, CL-P2T14-012, CL-P2T14-013, CL-P2T14-015, CL-P2T14-016, CL-P2T14-017, CL-P2T14-025, CL-P2T14-027, CL-P2T14-029, CL-P2T14-030, CL-P2T14-035; sources: S-T04-009, S-P2T14-004, S-P2T14-005, S-P2T14-009
- Strongest objection: Nelson’s reported distinction separates vivid memory from interpretation; REM intrusion/hypoxia is a possible alternative. Unknown timing and later information exposure undermine a uniquely survival-based inference.; strongest reply: Barker’s actual reply grants that brain states might be present yet argues correlates need not determine interpretation; first-person quality deserves consideration. This blocks an automatic dismissal but supplies no missing Neal measurements.
- Unresolved issues: Neural/circulatory timing; information exposure; independently preserved first witness report. No raw2013panel recording; actual reply is Barker’s, not Neal’s and not an empirical adjudication. General Mays rejoinder remains inherited broader debate, not direct corroboration. Named rescuer detail does not itself supply an independent first record; later hospital/PCU conversations are distinct from the river event.
- Review: P2R14 (accept)

#### A-P2T14-002 — Rescue interval and clinical inference (position: Audit a purported physiological exclusion)

- Premises: The memoir gives a reported eleven-to-fourteen-minute interval after missing-person headcounts; the SRT gives fifteen minutes after rescuers inferred the location; CNN calls the total an estimate., Available medical wording is narrator/reporter assertion; submersion, oxygen availability, circulation and neural state are different variables.
- Bridge principles: Elapsed rescue time alone cannot substitute for physiological measurement., A source saying it reviewed records does not make those originals inspected here.
- Conclusion: Retain testimony and reported recovery; withhold a synchronized medical reconstruction and specific process exclusion.
- Claims: CL-P2T14-007, CL-P2T14-008, CL-P2T14-009, CL-P2T14-019, CL-P2T14-020, CL-P2T14-021, CL-P2T14-025, CL-P2T14-027, CL-P2T14-028, CL-P2T14-031, CL-P2T14-036; sources: S-T04-009, S-P2T14-008, S-P2T14-002, S-P2T14-009
- Strongest objection: Neal identifies rescue-trained Long family members and reports listening to each individually, while the book gives a watch range and substantial injury detail. Those specific reports deserve assessment and could guide public corroboration.; strongest reply: The actual versions differ in timing and start events; no original timekeeper account resolves them. Specific testimony is not a synchronized physiological record. Later reported saturation or no-injury assertions do not date river awareness to absent neural function.
- Unresolved issues: Conflicting exact accident dates and age; no original timekeeper. No temperature/chart/EEG or medication record; no private requests authorized. ICU and river differ; later complaints/testing are not a single synchronous outcome. Memoir eleven-to-fourteen versus SRT fifteen minutes; memoir hospital values remain unverified and distinct from river physiology.
- Review: P2R14 (accept)

#### A-P2T14-003 — Prediction, fulfillment and prior documentation (position: Test foreknowledge without retrospective scoring)

- Premises: Neal retrospectively reports knowing her oldest son would die., Dated newspaper reporting supports a2009death report, while inspected prediction disclosure is later., No inspected independent record fixes prediction wording, deadline, cause and scoring set beforehand., The memoir narrates early disclosure and a pre-notification manuscript save, but also uses inconsistent first/final draft labels; its distinct child-not-eighteen story is not literally fulfilled within the same account.
- Bridge principles: Independent fulfillment does not date or validate a prediction., Absence of a retrieved advance record is an access limit, not proof no such record exists., Repeated assertions and river/ICU conversations cannot be summed as independent successes.
- Conclusion: Retain attributed prediction and documented reporting chronology; withhold verified foreknowledge and odds.
- Claims: CL-P2T14-004, CL-P2T14-005, CL-P2T14-010, CL-P2T14-018, CL-P2T14-022, CL-P2T14-023, CL-P2T14-024, CL-P2T14-030, CL-P2T14-032, CL-P2T14-033, CL-P2T14-034; sources: S-T04-009, S-P2T14-003, S-P2T14-008, S-P2T14-009
- Strongest objection: The strongest countercase to a successful-prediction reading combines postevent access to all detailed accounts, missing predated wording/scoring, internally different manuscript labels, and the separate age-specific child prediction followed by a changed-plan interpretation. Unknown counts prevent a rate calculation in either direction.; strongest reply: Neal reports early confidants and a manuscript before learning of the death, and interprets some foreknowledge as involving changeable plans. These are meaningful positive claims to preserve, but presently only retrospective; a flexible-plan reply needs a prior scoring rule to establish predictive accuracy.
- Unresolved issues: Original 2011 edition and any independent prefulfillment manuscript/confidant record remain uninspected. 2012-version spring first draft/final June21 versus Q&A first complete draft labels are unresolved. Child prediction is distinct from Neal’s directive and is not an externally verified failure count. All numeric prediction values remain null.
- Review: P2R14 (accept)

## Task P2T15 (narrative: work/P2T15/report.md)

### Arguments (3)

#### A-P2T15-001 — Alexander’s conditional cortical-exclusion and veridical-detail argument (position: Strongest developed defender, reconstructed without endorsing premises)

- Premises: Rich structured experience was remembered., Severe illness and alleged cortical incapacity are offered to exclude brain production., Specific faces and later photo recognition are offered as corroboration.
- Bridge principles: Accurate retrospective placement coincides with independently measured exclusion of the processes required by the targeted model., Relevant information was unavailable through ordinary routes.
- Conclusion: Conditional pressure on a specified brain-production account; unconditional survival/creator conclusion not established.
- Claims: CL-P2T15-006, CL-P2T15-007, CL-P2T15-008, CL-P2T15-010, CL-P2T15-012, CL-P2T15-014, CL-P2T15-015, CL-P2T15-016, CL-P2T15-017, CL-P2T15-018, CL-P2T15-019, CL-P2T15-020; sources: S-T06-006, S-P2T15-004, S-T06-002, S-T06-004
- Strongest objection: A-P2T15-002: timing, residual/recovering function and information-access bridges are unverified.; strongest reply: AppendixB and Mays appeal to severity, elaborate interactive recall, recovery phenomenological contrast and corroborative testimony; these deserve inspection.
- Unresolved issues: No continuous neural measurement; no whole-experience time lock; no blinded pre-photo record. Even brain independence would not establish timelessness, same-person survival, universal ground or perfect goodness.
- Review: P2R15 (accept)

#### A-P2T15-002 — Underdetermination of cause and time (position: Serious direct criticism plus author audit of evidence limits)

- Premises: Dittrich reports responsiveness/sedation; underlying interview disputed., The clinical reviewers cannot partition illness and drug effects., Memoir itself limits most temporal simultaneity to conjecture.
- Bridge principles: Excluding a mechanism requires relevant synchronized evidence; inability to provide one settled ordinary mechanism does not establish another.
- Conclusion: Specific ordinary and nonordinary causes remain underdetermined.
- Claims: CL-P2T15-012, CL-P2T15-014, CL-P2T15-015, CL-P2T15-021, CL-P2T15-023, CL-P2T15-029, CL-P2T15-030, CL-P2T15-032; sources: S-T06-003, S-T06-002, S-T06-006
- Strongest objection: A-P2T15-001: exceptionally severe impairment and matching details might challenge ordinary production if independently established.; strongest reply: Retain those positive reports, distinguish absence of accessible evidence from evidence of absence, and state exactly which timing/function/acquisition tests remain unmet.
- Unresolved issues: No diagnosis of hallucination/fraud from this audit. Other critic chains, original tapes/charts and historical webpage snapshots uninspected.
- Review: P2R15 (accept)

#### A-P2T15-003 — Mays’s actual reply to a solely pharmacological account (position: Narrow direct reply with later clinical comparison)

- Premises: Mays rejects sedation alone and cites Wade plus attributed Potter context., Memoir acknowledges both illness and sedative use., Clinical review reports pre-sedation impairment but uncertain later mixture.
- Bridge principles: Illness and treatment may jointly affect responsiveness; contextual journalism cannot by itself settle physiology.
- Conclusion: Drug-only dismissal is unsupported by this packet; rejecting it does not prove a cortex-free experience.
- Claims: CL-P2T15-010, CL-P2T15-011, CL-P2T15-012, CL-P2T15-021, CL-P2T15-022, CL-P2T15-023, CL-P2T15-024, CL-P2T15-025; sources: S-T06-004, S-T06-003, S-T06-002, S-P2T15-004, S-T06-006
- Strongest objection: Potter statement is mediated, removed at request, and unsupported by original tape; memoir timing/clinical figures differ.; strongest reply: Wade’s separately signed account and published record-review account strengthen illness attribution but retain the causal/timing limits.
- Unresolved issues: No wholesale validation of Mays’s final metaphysical assurance. Mays79–84 fully read as rhetoric/career context; original video/legal materials not authenticated.
- Review: P2R15 (accept)

### Arguments (3)

#### A-P2T17-001 — Conditional unusual-cart and pre-Thumper argument (position: Strongest bounded extracerebral-perception case reconstructed from defenders)

- Premises: TG reports a patient description of an unusual cart and wooden shelf., TG’s direct reply places removal before switching on the Thumper., Defenders infer ordinary visual/auditory acquisition was unavailable.

A generic appeal to hearing does not itself explain every unusual detail.

#### A-P2T17-003 — Dependency and nine-component boundary (position: Methodological inference)

- Bridge principles: Reports, observed events and inferred causes must be assessed separately; no automatic component bridge.
- Conclusion: Append source/version and chronology qualifications to C-T19-001 while retaining all twelve gates and nine component distinctions.
- Claims: CL-P2T17-002, CL-P2T17-020, CL-P2T17-025, CL-P2T17-028, CL-P2T17-029, CL-P2T17-030; sources: S-T19-002, S-T19-004, S-P2T17-003, S-P2T17-007
- Strongest objection: A credible detailed witness report can still have evidential value without being a prospective target experiment.; strongest reply: The packet retains that conditional value and the specific cart challenge while declining unsupported extrapolations.
- Unresolved issues: No numerical posterior; no pooled denominator; other conceptual routes remain outside scope.
- Review: P2R17 (accept)

## Task P2T18 (narrative: work/P2T18/report.md)

### Arguments (3)

#### A-P2T18-001 — Historical recurrence and the prospective report: strongest bounded positive case (position: Conditional relevance to an experiential phenomenon and to better tests of H-B)

- Premises: CL-P2T18-001, CL-P2T18-002, CL-P2T18-004, CL-P2T18-005, CL-P2T18-009, CL-P2T18-010, CL-P2T18-011, CL-P2T18-017, CL-P2T18-022
- Bridge principles: A documented nineteenth-century narrative weakens the claim that every such motif was invented after modern NDE publicity, provided later translation and source transmission are not counted as new reports., Prospective recruitment strengthens the temporal definition of a study sample; it does not independently timestamp the origin of a later recalled experience., A stronger brain-independence inference requires content-specific timing, specified neural-exclusion criteria and independently controlled information access.
- Conclusion: This selected corpus and pilot justify investigating recurring reported experiences, without establishing a unique cause, global recurrence rate or brain independence.
- Claims: CL-P2T18-001, CL-P2T18-002, CL-P2T18-004, CL-P2T18-005, CL-P2T18-009, CL-P2T18-010, CL-P2T18-011, CL-P2T18-017, CL-P2T18-022, CL-P2T18-028, CL-P2T18-031; sources: S-P2T18-001, S-P2T18-003, S-T08-005
- Strongest objection: European literary/reporting dependence, unmeasured historical danger states, selected survivors, unknown target opportunities and bodily-awareness coding can generate misleading convergence.; strongest reply: Those limitations do not erase the dated reports or show every account was fabricated or normally explained. A constrained hypothesis can still seek evidence that alternatives predict differently.
- Unresolved issues: Exact published translation and Fraktur visual verification No non-Western expansion No content-linked neural exclusion, irreversible-death subjectivity or same-person survival
- Review: P2R18 (accept)

#### A-P2T18-002 — Controlled-target countercase and actual exchange (position: Challenges overinterpretation of veridicality evidence; does not establish a physicalist winner)

- Premises: CL-P2T18-012, CL-P2T18-013, CL-P2T18-018, CL-P2T18-019, CL-P2T18-020, CL-P2T18-021, CL-P2T18-032, CL-P2T18-033, CL-P2T18-034, CL-P2T18-035
- Bridge principles: A target test bears negatively on a specified ability only when enough genuine opportunities and an appropriate expectation of identification are established., Possible sensory or reporting errors block claims that such routes are excluded; possibility alone does not demonstrate their occurrence., Antecedent probabilities require independent justification and are not supplied by author agreement or a source-quality rating.
- Conclusion: The selected Parnia reports provide no validated concealed-target success and no verified effective-trial denominator. Neither the target null nor the unresolved ordinary-route alternatives settle the metaphysical dispute.
- Claims: CL-P2T18-012, CL-P2T18-013, CL-P2T18-018, CL-P2T18-019, CL-P2T18-020, CL-P2T18-021, CL-P2T18-032, CL-P2T18-033, CL-P2T18-034, CL-P2T18-035; sources: S-P2T18-003, S-P2T18-004, S-P2T18-005, S-P2T18-006, S-P2T18-007
- Strongest objection: Greyson argues that untested error possibilities should not outweigh reports and cited stability evidence; he disputes Augustine’s treatment of paranormal-feature stability and default priors.; strongest reply: Augustine concedes possibility is not actuality and small target numbers are inconclusive, but demands evidence excluding ordinary information routes. The project accepts that evidential requirement without adopting his unmeasured causal verdict or twelve-case denominator.
- Unresolved issues: Parnia no-OBE prose conflicts with Greyson four-case attribution and Augustine’s later repeated dozen Longitudinal original not independently inspected; no global memory-fidelity conclusion Target exposure/interview/viewpoint intersection unknown
- Review: P2R18 (accept)

#### A-P2T18-003 — Measurement and dependence countercase (position: Limits pooled cultural and prospective convergence)

- Premises: CL-P2T18-003, CL-P2T18-007, CL-P2T18-014, CL-P2T18-015, CL-P2T18-023, CL-P2T18-024, CL-P2T18-025, CL-P2T18-026, CL-P2T18-027, CL-P2T18-028, CL-P2T18-029, CL-P2T18-030
- Bridge principles: Analytic reuse of four reports is a repeated use of existing evidence, not four new observations., Item labels must preserve response wording and score thresholds; a body-awareness score does not imply a visual vantage or target opportunity., Unknown participant overlap cannot be replaced by either complete disjointness or total duplication., Nonsignificance, unasked items and absent reports do not respectively imply equivalence, absent experience and absent consciousness.
- Conclusion: Use a nonadditive, source-qualified comparison; preserve all old numbers and unknowns while adding exact reuse and wording qualifications.
- Claims: CL-P2T18-003, CL-P2T18-007, CL-P2T18-014, CL-P2T18-015, CL-P2T18-023, CL-P2T18-024, CL-P2T18-025, CL-P2T18-026, CL-P2T18-027, CL-P2T18-028, CL-P2T18-029, CL-P2T18-030; sources: S-P2T18-001, S-P2T18-003, S-T08-005
- Strongest objection: Recurring motifs across times and conditions may reflect a common phenomenon even when instruments differ; documenting dependence is not a causal explanation of every case.; strongest reply: That possibility remains. Distinctive support requires comparable ascertainment and predictions that survive the stated coding/overlap uncertainties. Neither cultural nor neural mechanisms are established by bookkeeping.
- Unresolved issues: Unknown invitation frame and participant identities Translation and omitted cultural corpus gaps No validated global denominator or numerical metaphysical likelihood
- Review: P2R18 (accept)

#### C-T07-003 — AWARE II ancillary cross-sectional community arm (study)

- Underlying event/sample: Community survivors submitted narratives by mail or were identified from a public NDERF database using CPR/defibrillation history.
